**Executive summary.** Mal's three payment squads (Cards, Transfers, Bill Payments) ship into three schemas, three databases, and three sets of squad-specific reports. Finance reconciliation, Customer 360, and CBUAE corridor reporting all suffer. Two known reconciliation incidents have been traced to float rounding in Cards. We propose one canonical event-grain Parquet store, quarantine-pattern validation, and a 24-week, four-phase migration that lands each squad with zero blast radius in Phase 0 and a mechanical cutover by Phase 2. D1 is a working 449-line implementation with 24 tests passing. D3 is the on-call data-quality dashboard. The biggest risk is adoption, not technology; Phase 0 is what de-risks it.

## Context

Mal is a UAE neobank with Islamic banking products. Three squads own three payment surfaces: **Cards** (auth/capture lifecycle, MCC-tagged merchants, mostly AED with some USD/GBP), **Transfers** (domestic plus expat-driven remittance corridors to India, Philippines, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Egypt), and **Bill Payments** (utilities, telecom, government, scheduled vs executed). Each squad ships into its own database; there is no cross-product event store today.

| Stakeholder | Pain today |
|:----|:------------|
| Finance reconciliation | Three pipelines, manual joins, two known float rounding incidents in Cards |
| Customer Success | No cross-product customer view; `customer_id` semantics differ across two of three squads |
| Compliance, CBUAE reporting | Corridor volume sits in Transfers; failure-code vocabulary differs from Cards; no shared audit trail |
| Platform reliability | No single dashboard for "all payment failures last 7 days"; each squad has its own status vocabulary |

## Target architecture

![Target architecture: five layers, one canonical store](img/target_architecture.png){width=78% fig-pos="!ht"}

Five load-bearing decisions, each a direct response to a real failure mode.

**1. Event-grain, not payment-grain.** auth, capture, and refund are one logical payment but multiple events linked by `correlation_id`. The auth-to-settle latency query in D1 (SQL 03) cannot be written cleanly on squad-grained data.

**2. Integer minor units.** `amount_minor` parsed at the squad boundary using `decimal.Decimal` with banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN). The v1 to v2 migration in `schema/migrations.py` is the recovery path for v1 data already in flight.

**3. raw_payload preserved per row.** Squads do not lose information when they hand data to the platform. This is an adoption lever, not a technical one. Auditability comes for free.

**4. payment_method_details as a JSON bag.** When the Wallet squad ships in Q3, we add an adapter, not a schema migration. Bounds the cost of a new payment type to one file.

**5. Quarantine, not fail-fast.** Bad rows from one squad never block another. Quarantine files preserve the original payload plus the validation error. Pipeline exits zero even with quarantined records; non-zero is reserved for infrastructure failures.

## Migration strategy

![Migration timeline: 24 weeks across four phases](img/migration_timeline.png){width=78% fig-pos="!ht"}

**Phase 0, shadow mode (weeks 1 to 4).** Adapters read squad data and write to the canonical store. Squad systems unchanged. Daily delta report; zero blast radius. Exit when delta report is green for two consecutive weeks and the squad PM signs off on the failure-code mapping.

**Phase 1, dual-write (weeks 5 to 8).** Squads dual-write via the adapter. Finance and Customer Success cut over to read from the canonical store. Squad-specific dashboards keep working. Exit when both consumers accept canonical as primary.

**Phase 2, cutover (weeks 9 to 12).** Squad-specific reports decommissioned with a 30-day grace window. CBUAE reports run off canonical. Squads keep their transactional databases; canonical is the analytics source of truth.

**Phase 3, schema convergence (weeks 13 to 24).** Optional. Where the squad PM agrees, transactional schemas start adopting canonical fields. The platform does not block on this. The v1 to v2 migration in D1 is the template for any future schema bump: defaults for legacy rows, banker's rounding on numerics, every output row revalidated, source data never mutated, idempotent on rerun.

## Production readiness

D1 was scoped for a 30-second local run. At Mal's expected production volume of around 100K transactions per day, the following gaps matter.

| Gap | What D1 does | What production needs | Priority |
|:----|:-------------|:---------------------|:--------:|
| Orchestration | One Python process | Dagster: asset-based DAG, SQL sensors, lineage UI for CBUAE audit | `\hi`{=latex}`<span class="prio-high">High</span>`{=html} |
| Ingestion | CSV files in `data/raw/` | Debezium plus Kafka for CDC, 30-second freshness SLO, replay support | `\hi`{=latex}`<span class="prio-high">High</span>`{=html} |
| Customer identity | `customer_id` trusted from each squad | Identity service deduplicating across phone, email, national ID | `\hi`{=latex}`<span class="prio-high">High</span>`{=html} |
| PII tokenization | `last4` only, no real PII in mocks | Vault or KMS for tokens; analytics never sees raw PII | `\hi`{=latex}`<span class="prio-high">High</span>`{=html} |
| Observability | One INFO line per squad per run | Structured logging, per-stage metrics, alerts on quarantine spikes | `\hi`{=latex}`<span class="prio-high">High</span>`{=html} |
| Schema registry | Pydantic models in the repo | Confluent or Git-based registry with evolution rules | `\md`{=latex}`<span class="prio-med">Medium</span>`{=html} |
| Multi-region DR | Single local Parquet directory | UAE-resident primary, second region for DR (CBUAE residency) | `\md`{=latex}`<span class="prio-med">Medium</span>`{=html} |
| Backfill, replay | Re-run `make seed` and `make run` | Replay-from-Kafka with idempotent writes, Dagster backfill jobs | `\md`{=latex}`<span class="prio-med">Medium</span>`{=html} |
| Dashboards | GitHub Pages report, Streamlit (D3) | Looker or Superset on the canonical store, squad-specific saved views | `\md`{=latex}`<span class="prio-med">Medium</span>`{=html} |
| FX rates | Hardcoded USD, AED, GBP | Price-service integration with timestamped rates and audit trail | `\md`{=latex}`<span class="prio-med">Medium</span>`{=html} |

: Production gap punch list {tbl-colwidths="[18, 24, 46, 12]"}

The High items are non-negotiable for a production launch. Medium items can land iteratively after the canonical store is live. None of them change the canonical model.

## Risk register

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|:-----|:-----------|:-------|:------------|
| Squad PM deprioritizes Phase 0 onboarding | Medium | High | Phase 0 has zero blast radius; squad does no work; we run the adapter against their export |
| Vocabulary mapping disputes between squads | Medium | Medium | Mapping owned by platform team; disputes escalate to one Director |
| Customer identity collisions across squads | High | High | Identity service is a Phase 1 dependency, not a Phase 0 blocker |
| CBUAE residency requirements bite mid-rollout | Low | High | UAE-resident object store from day one; DR region designed in, not retrofit |
| Adapter coverage gap in production | Medium | Medium | Quarantine pattern catches it; daily quarantine-rate alert on D3 catches the spike |

## Success metrics

**Adoption (lagging).** Three squads on canonical by week 12; 100% finance recon; 80% squad reports retired. **Quality (leading).** Quarantine under 2% per squad; zero unannounced schema-drift per quarter; recon delta under 0.01% by row, exact by amount; surfaced live on D3. **Performance.** Freshness 30s p95; daily backfill under 10 min at 100K txn/day; 99.9% monthly availability.
